addFeature.doc: Insert a new feature. Its ids must be fresh and cannot be split pieces; `index` defaults to the rollback bar.

editFeature.doc: Replace a feature's inputs. Same id and kind; ids it introduces must be fresh, and a split piece must split an id this feature had before and no longer has.

deleteFeature.doc: Remove a feature. Refused while another feature depends on it.

restoreFeature.doc: Put an earlier state of a feature back (undo of a delete or an edit, and redo of an add). Replaces the feature with the same id, or inserts it at `index`, and sets the rollback bar. Unlike `addFeature` and `editFeature`, its ids must have been allocated before. History only: it is the inverse that undo and redo apply, and it checks only that each id was allocated at some point, not that a split piece is fresh. Clients editing a feature use `editFeature`, which enforces the full id rules.

reorderFeature.doc: Move a feature so it ends up at `index`. Refused if it would pass a dependency.

setMaterial.doc: Set what the part's body is made of (a built-in material id), or clear it with `null`.

setBodyProps.doc: Set a body's name, colour and material, all at once: `props` replaces the body's entry, and empty `props` removes it. `index` places a new entry (default: last); ignored on update.

setBodyGroup.doc: Create or replace a body group of the part, by id: its name and its bodies. A new group needs a fresh `group#n` id from the part's `nextIds.group` and goes at `index` (default: last); `index` is ignored on replace. A body is in at most one group of its part, so moving a body between groups is a batch of two. Since version 17.

deleteBodyGroup.doc: Remove a body group. Its bodies stay as they are. Since version 17.

restoreBodyGroup.doc: History only: put a deleted body group back at `index` (its id was allocated before).

setRollback.doc: Move the rollback bar; `null` puts it after the last feature.

setVariable.doc: Create or update a variable. `index` places a new one (default: last); ignored on update.

deleteVariable.doc: Remove a variable. Refused while a variable or feature references it.

setDisplayUnits.doc: Change display units. Stored expressions keep their own units, so no geometry changes.

setConfigParameter.doc: Create or replace a configuration parameter, by id. A new one needs a fresh `cp#n` id and goes at `index` (default: last); `index` is ignored on replace.

deleteConfigParameter.doc: Remove a configuration parameter and every row's value for it.

restoreConfigParameter.doc: History only: put a deleted parameter back at `index` (its id was allocated before).

setConfigRow.doc: Create or replace a configuration row, by id. A new one needs a fresh `cfg#n` id and goes at `index` (default: last); `index` is ignored on replace.

deleteConfigRow.doc: Remove a configuration row. Deleting the active row leaves no row active.

restoreConfigRow.doc: History only: put a deleted row back at `index` (its id was allocated before).

setActiveConfiguration.doc: Choose the row the document is shown and built in; `null`: none.

addPart.doc: Add an empty part studio. `partId` must be a fresh `part#n` from the document's `nextIds.part`; it goes at `index` (default: last).

renamePart.doc: Rename a part studio (trimmed, 1 to 200 characters).

deletePart.doc: Remove a part studio. Refused for the last one, while a configuration parameter suppresses one of its features, while an assembly instance shows it, and while a print item prints it.

restorePart.doc: History only: put a deleted part studio back at `index` (undo of a delete, redo of an add or a duplicate). Its id must have been allocated before; the counter does not move.

reorderParts.doc: Move a part studio so it ends up at `index`.

duplicatePart.doc: Copy part studio `sourcePartId` to a new one, `partId` (a fresh `part#n`), at `index` (default: just after the source). Features keep their ids, since ids are per part; body names, colours and materials, the rollback bar and the counters are copied too.

addAssembly.doc: Add an empty assembly. `assemblyId` must be a fresh `assembly#n` from the document's `nextIds.assembly`; it goes at `index` (default: last).

deleteAssembly.doc: Remove an assembly with its instances and mates. Nothing else refers to an assembly.

restoreAssembly.doc: History only: put a deleted assembly back at `index` (its id was allocated before).

addInstance.doc: Add an instance, last. Its id must be a fresh `inst#n` from the assembly's `nextIds.inst`; a part of this document must exist.

editInstance.doc: Change an instance's name, `fixed`, `suppressed`, shown `bodies` (`null`: every body) or `source` (another part or pin, or another configuration row). Absent fields stay.

setPoses.doc: Set the poses of several instances at once, by instance id: one undo step for a solve or a drag. Commit on drag end and after mate edits, never per frame.

deleteInstance.doc: Remove an instance. Refused while a mate connects it.

restoreInstance.doc: History only: put a deleted instance back at `index` (its id was allocated before).

addMate.doc: Add a mate, last (the newest). Its id, its connectors' ids and their references' ids must be fresh (`mate#n`, `mc#n`, `r<n>` from the assembly's `nextIds`).

editMate.doc: Replace a mate's inputs, by id. Ids it introduces must be fresh.

deleteMate.doc: Remove a mate with its connectors.

restoreMate.doc: History only: put a mate state back, replacing the mate with the same id (at `index`) or inserting it at `index`. Its ids must have been allocated before.

addPrintSetup.doc: Add a print setup at `index` (default: last). Its id, its items' ids and their references' ids must be fresh (`print#n`, `item#n`, `r<n>` from `print.nextIds`). Since version 8.

editPrintSetup.doc: Change a setup's name, printer, nozzle or thresholds (`null`: the defaults). Absent fields stay. Items are edited with the item commands.

deletePrintSetup.doc: Remove a print setup with its items. Nothing refers to a setup.

restorePrintSetup.doc: History only: put a deleted setup back at `index` (its ids were allocated before).

addPrintItem.doc: Add an item to a setup at `index` (default: last). Its id and its face reference's id must be fresh (`item#n`, `r<n>` from `print.nextIds`); the part must exist. The body and face are not checked against the part: what they name may change or go, and the print workspace reports it.

editPrintItem.doc: Replace an item's inputs, by id. Ids it introduces must be fresh.

deletePrintItem.doc: Remove an item from a setup.

restorePrintItem.doc: History only: put an item state back, replacing the item with the same id (at `index`) or inserting it at `index`. Its ids must have been allocated before.

addFont.doc: Add a font at `index` (default: last). Its id must be a fresh `font#n` from the document's `nextIds.font`; a font with the same bytes (SHA-256) may not be added twice. Since version 9.

deleteFont.doc: Remove a font. Refused while an outline of any sketch uses it.

restoreFont.doc: History only: put a deleted font back at `index` (its id was allocated before).

setScript.doc: Create or replace a script of the library, by id (ADR 0010 decision 8). A new one needs a fresh `script#n` id from the document's `nextIds.script` and goes at `index` (default: last); `index` is ignored on replace. Replacing a script changes every scripted feature that runs it. Since version 16.

deleteScript.doc: Remove a script. Refused while a scripted feature of any part runs it. Since version 16.

restoreScript.doc: History only: put a deleted script back at `index` (its id was allocated before).

setDomainData.doc: Replace a domain's document-level data (ADR 0013 decision 3): `schemaVersion` and `data` together set the namespace's entry; both absent remove it. Core never looks inside `data`; the domain package validates it before issuing the command. The inverse sets the old entry back, or removes the namespace when it had none. Since version 11.

addExplodedView.doc: Add an exploded view to an assembly at `index` (default: last). Its id and its steps' ids must be fresh (`explode#n`, `step#n` from the assembly's `nextIds`). Since version 12.

editExplodedView.doc: Replace an exploded view's name and steps, by id: renaming it, and adding, editing, removing or reordering steps in one go. Ids it introduces must be fresh.

deleteExplodedView.doc: Remove an exploded view with its steps. Refused while a drawing view shows it.

restoreExplodedView.doc: History only: put an exploded view state back, replacing the one with the same id (at `index`) or inserting it at `index`. Its ids must have been allocated before.

addExplodeStep.doc: Add a step to an exploded view at `index` (default: last). Its id must be a fresh `step#n`.

editExplodeStep.doc: Replace a step's instances, direction and distance, by id.

deleteExplodeStep.doc: Remove a step. Nothing refers to a step.

restoreExplodeStep.doc: History only: put a step state back (replace by id at `index`, or insert at `index`).

addDrawing.doc: Add a drawing at `index` (default: last). Its id must be a fresh `drawing#n` from the document's `nextIds.drawing`; the ids inside it must be allocated by its own `nextIds`. Since version 12.

deleteDrawing.doc: Remove a drawing with its sheets. Nothing refers to a drawing.

restoreDrawing.doc: History only: put a deleted drawing back at `index` (its id was allocated before).

reorderDrawings.doc: Move a drawing so it ends up at `index`.

addSheet.doc: Add a sheet to a drawing at `index` (default: last). Its id and the ids of its views, dimensions and notes must be fresh (`sheet#n`, `view#n`, `dim#n`, `note#n` from the drawing's `nextIds`).

editSheet.doc: Change a sheet's name, size, orientation or title block (`null`: none). Absent fields stay. Views, dimensions and notes are edited with their own commands.

deleteSheet.doc: Remove a sheet with its views, dimensions and notes. Nothing outside the sheet refers to it.

restoreSheet.doc: History only: put a deleted sheet back at `index` (its ids were allocated before).

reorderSheets.doc: Move a sheet so it ends up at `index`.

addView.doc: Add a view to a sheet at `index` (default: last). Its id must be a fresh `view#n` from the drawing's `nextIds`; the part, assembly or exploded view it shows must exist.

editView.doc: Replace a view's inputs, by id (source, direction, scale, position, options, label).

moveView.doc: Move a view on its sheet (a drag): set its `position` only.

deleteView.doc: Remove a view. Refused while a dimension or note on the sheet is in it.

restoreView.doc: History only: put a view state back (replace by id at `index`, or insert at `index`).

addDimension.doc: Add a dimension to a sheet at `index` (default: last). Its id must be a fresh `dim#n` from the drawing's `nextIds`; its view must be on the sheet. Its model references are not checked against the model: what they name may change or go, and regen reports it.

editDimension.doc: Replace a dimension's inputs, by id (a re-pick, a drag of its placement, a text override).

restoreDimension.doc: History only: put a dimension state back (replace by id at `index`, or insert at `index`).

addNote.doc: Add a note to a sheet at `index` (default: last). Its id must be a fresh `note#n`.

editNote.doc: Replace a note's text, position or view, by id.

restoreNote.doc: History only: put a note state back (replace by id at `index`, or insert at `index`).

addCamTool.doc: Add a CAM tool at `index` (default: last). Its id must be a fresh `tool#n` from `cam.nextIds`. Since version 14.

editCamTool.doc: Replace a tool's inputs, by id.

deleteCamTool.doc: Remove a tool. Refused while an operation of any setup cuts with it.

restoreCamTool.doc: History only: put a tool state back (replace by id at `index`, or insert at `index`).

addCamSetup.doc: Add a CAM setup at `index` (default: last). Its id, its WCS face reference's and those of its operations must be fresh (`setup#n`, `<kind>#n`, `r<n>` from `cam.nextIds`); its part must exist and its operations' tools be in `cam.tools`. The body, faces, sketches and holes it names are not checked against the part (ADR 0014 decision 6).

editCamSetup.doc: Change a setup's name, part, body (`null`: the part's only body), machine, post, stock, WCS or heights. Absent fields stay; operations are edited with their own commands. A new WCS face reference id must be fresh.

deleteCamSetup.doc: Remove a setup with its operations. Nothing refers to a setup.

restoreCamSetup.doc: History only: put a setup state back, replacing the setup with the same id (at `index`) or inserting it at `index`. Its ids must have been allocated before.

reorderCamSetups.doc: Move a setup so it ends up at `index`.

addCamOperation.doc: Add an operation to a setup at `index` (default: last, the end of the cut order). Its id and its face references' ids must be fresh (`<kind>#n`, `r<n>` from `cam.nextIds`); its tool must be in `cam.tools`.

editCamOperation.doc: Replace an operation's inputs, by id (so of the same kind). Ids it introduces must be fresh.

deleteCamOperation.doc: Remove an operation from a setup. Nothing refers to an operation.

restoreCamOperation.doc: History only: put an operation state back, replacing the one with the same id (at `index`) or inserting it at `index`. Its ids must have been allocated before. With `deleteCamOperation` in one batch, it moves an operation to another setup under its id.

reorderCamOperation.doc: Move an operation so it ends up at `index` in its setup's cut order.

setMechRequirements.doc: Replace the mechanical requirements (ADR 0017 decision 10), as a whole list in table order. Ids it introduces must be fresh `req#n` from `mech.nextIds`. An empty list removes them. What a requirement names (a load case, a drivetrain, a record) is not checked: a missing one is the domain's warning. Since version 19.

restoreMechRequirements.doc: History only: put a requirements list back (its ids were allocated before).

setElectrical.doc: Replace the electrical system (ADR 0017 decision 11): components with their diagram nudges, connections and harness segments. Ids it introduces must be fresh (`el#n`, `conn#n`, `seg#n` from `mech.nextIds`). With no components, connections or segments it removes the system. Since version 19.

restoreElectrical.doc: History only: put an electrical system back (its ids were allocated before).

setMechLoadCase.doc: Create or replace a load case of the mechanical section, by id (ADR 0017 decision 2). A new one goes at `index` (default: last); `index` is ignored on replace. Ids it introduces must be fresh: `lc#n` from `mech.nextIds`. Since version 19.

deleteMechLoadCase.doc: Remove a load case. Nothing refers to it in a way core checks. Since version 19.

restoreMechLoadCase.doc: History only: put a load case state back, replacing the one with the same id (at `index`) or inserting it at `index`. Its ids must have been allocated before.

setDrivetrain.doc: Create or replace a drivetrain of the mechanical section, by id (ADR 0017 decision 2). A new one goes at `index` (default: last); `index` is ignored on replace. Ids it introduces must be fresh: `drive#n` (its stages `stage#n`) from `mech.nextIds`. Since version 19.

deleteDrivetrain.doc: Remove a drivetrain. Nothing refers to it in a way core checks. Since version 19.

restoreDrivetrain.doc: History only: put a drivetrain state back, replacing the one with the same id (at `index`) or inserting it at `index`. Its ids must have been allocated before.

setPurchasedUse.doc: Create or replace a purchased part use of the mechanical section, by id (ADR 0017 decision 2). A new one goes at `index` (default: last); `index` is ignored on replace. Ids it introduces must be fresh: `pp#n` from `mech.nextIds`. Since version 19.

deletePurchasedUse.doc: Remove a purchased part use. Nothing refers to it in a way core checks. Since version 19.

restorePurchasedUse.doc: History only: put a purchased part use state back, replacing the one with the same id (at `index`) or inserting it at `index`. Its ids must have been allocated before.

setCatalogEntry.doc: Create or replace a user catalog entry of the mechanical section, by id (ADR 0017 decision 2). A new one goes at `index` (default: last); `index` is ignored on replace. Ids it introduces must be fresh: `entry#n` from `mech.nextIds`. Since version 19.

deleteCatalogEntry.doc: Remove a user catalog entry. Nothing refers to it in a way core checks. Since version 19.

restoreCatalogEntry.doc: History only: put a user catalog entry state back, replacing the one with the same id (at `index`) or inserting it at `index`. Its ids must have been allocated before.

setSchematic.doc: Create or replace a schematic of the mechanical section, by id (ADR 0017 decision 2). A new one goes at `index` (default: last); `index` is ignored on replace. Ids it introduces must be fresh: `sch#n` (its sheets, symbols, wires, labels, ports and notes `sheet#n`, `us#n`, `wire#n`, `label#n`, `port#n`, `text#n`) from `mech.nextIds`. Since version 19.

deleteSchematic.doc: Remove a schematic. Nothing refers to it in a way core checks. Since version 19.

restoreSchematic.doc: History only: put a schematic state back, replacing the one with the same id (at `index`) or inserting it at `index`. Its ids must have been allocated before.

setSymbol.doc: Create or replace a user symbol of the mechanical section, by id (ADR 0017 decision 2). A new one goes at `index` (default: last); `index` is ignored on replace. Ids it introduces must be fresh: `sym#n` from `mech.nextIds`. Since version 19.

deleteSymbol.doc: Remove a user symbol. Nothing refers to it in a way core checks. Since version 19.

restoreSymbol.doc: History only: put a user symbol state back, replacing the one with the same id (at `index`) or inserting it at `index`. Its ids must have been allocated before.

setStudy.doc: Create or replace a stress study of the mechanical section, by id (ADR 0017 decision 2). A new one goes at `index` (default: last); `index` is ignored on replace. Ids it introduces must be fresh: `study#n` (its face references `r<n>`) from `mech.nextIds`. Since version 19.

deleteStudy.doc: Remove a stress study. Nothing refers to it in a way core checks. Since version 19.

restoreStudy.doc: History only: put a stress study state back, replacing the one with the same id (at `index`) or inserting it at `index`. Its ids must have been allocated before.

setCheckOverride.doc: Create or replace a check override of the mechanical section, by id (ADR 0017 decision 2). A new one goes at `index` (default: last); `index` is ignored on replace. Ids it introduces must be fresh: `chk#n` from `mech.nextIds`. Since version 19.

deleteCheckOverride.doc: Remove a check override. Nothing refers to it in a way core checks. Since version 19.

restoreCheckOverride.doc: History only: put a check override state back, replacing the one with the same id (at `index`) or inserting it at `index`. Its ids must have been allocated before.

setSpecNote.doc: Create or replace a specification note of the mechanical section, by id (ADR 0017 decision 2). A new one goes at `index` (default: last); `index` is ignored on replace. Ids it introduces must be fresh: `note#n` from `mech.nextIds`. Since version 19.

deleteSpecNote.doc: Remove a specification note. Nothing refers to it in a way core checks. Since version 19.

restoreSpecNote.doc: History only: put a specification note state back, replacing the one with the same id (at `index`) or inserting it at `index`. Its ids must have been allocated before.

setHazard.doc: Create or replace a hazard of the mechanical section, by id (ADR 0017 decision 2). A new one goes at `index` (default: last); `index` is ignored on replace. Ids it introduces must be fresh: `hz#n` from `mech.nextIds`. Since version 19.

deleteHazard.doc: Remove a hazard. Nothing refers to it in a way core checks. Since version 19.

restoreHazard.doc: History only: put a hazard state back, replacing the one with the same id (at `index`) or inserting it at `index`. Its ids must have been allocated before.

setTestBand.doc: Create or replace a test band of the mechanical section, by id (ADR 0017 decision 2). A new one goes at `index` (default: last); `index` is ignored on replace. Ids it introduces must be fresh: `vt#n` from `mech.nextIds`. Since version 19.

deleteTestBand.doc: Remove a test band. Nothing refers to it in a way core checks. Since version 19.

restoreTestBand.doc: History only: put a test band state back, replacing the one with the same id (at `index`) or inserting it at `index`. Its ids must have been allocated before.

setMaterialDef.doc: Create or replace a user material (ADR 0017 decision 4), by id. A new one needs a fresh `material#n` from the document's `nextIds.material` and goes at `index` (default: last); `index` is ignored on replace. Its values are constants of their properties' kinds. Since version 19.

deleteMaterialDef.doc: Remove a user material. Refused while a part or a body uses it. Since version 19.

restoreMaterialDef.doc: History only: put a deleted user material back at `index` (its id was allocated before).

replaceDocument.doc: History only: put a whole document in place of this one (restore a version or revision; the undo of a restore). The replacement must be this document (same `id`) and valid as a whole, assemblies and configurations included. Its inverse is `replaceDocument` of the document it replaced. Clients restoring an older state build the replacement with `restoredDocument`, which keeps the id counters from going back.

fields.draft: Draft angle: positive tapers the sides inward along the extrusion, negative outward. The neutral plane is the sketch plane. Absent means no draft.
fields.scope: The bodies the operation combines with; absent: every body. Not for a `new` extrude.

fields.symmetric: Split the angle evenly to both sides of the sketch plane.
fields.scope: The bodies the operation combines with; absent: every body. Not for a `new` revolve.

fields.distance: Along the reference face of each edge: the adjacent face whose name sorts first (T1.8). Equal chamfers measure it on both faces.
fields.secondDistance: Unequal chamfer: the distance along the other face. Absent means equal distances.
fields.angle: Distance-angle chamfer: the angle from the reference face. Excludes `secondDistance`.

fields.faces: Faces to remove (open the shell); may be empty for a closed hollow.
fields.outward: Grow the wall outward instead of inward.

fields.sketch: The sketch whose points place the holes, drilled along its normal.
fields.extent: How deep: `blind` to `depth` (to the shoulder, where the wall ends), or `throughAll`. A blind hole ends in a drill point of `tipAngle` (an angle, more than 0 and at most 180 deg; absent: 118 deg); 180 deg is a flat bottom, as for a heat-set insert. `tipAngle` since version 18.
fields.standard: What the hole was sized for: a screw's clearance hole (`{ size, fit }`: `M6`, `#10`, `1/4` from the kernel's `HOLE_SIZES`), or since version 18 a heat-set insert (`{ size, purpose: 'heat-set-insert' }`: `M2` to `M5` from packages/print's `HEAT_SET_INSERTS`, whose hole is the diameter, whose length is the least depth, and whose minimum wall goes with the size). Informational: `diameter`, the depth and the head sizes are what regen uses, so a standard hole can still be edited by hand.
fields.scope: The bodies the holes are drilled into; absent: every body.

fields.body: Repeat the bodies instead of features.
fields.scope: With `body: true`, the bodies to copy; absent: every body.
fields.mode: With `body: true`, how the copies join the part; absent: `add`. Since version 6.

fields.body: Mirror the bodies instead of features.
fields.scope: With `body: true`, the bodies to mirror; absent: every body.
fields.mode: With `body: true`, how the copies join the part; absent: `add`. Since version 6.

extension.doc: The extension point for domain features (woodworking, construction; ADR 0013). `extension` is a dotted, namespaced type (`wood.board`) with its own `schemaVersion`, owned by the domain package. Core understands only the generic parts: feature dependencies, geometry references, expressions, and since version 11 `operation` and `scope`, which it validates like any other feature's. `params` is opaque JSON.

fields.operation: How the extension's solid combines with the part, as for an extrude: with `new` or `add` the extension creates bodies (`extension#n`, or `extension#n:<key>` for several). Absent: it makes no solid of its own to combine. Since version 11.
fields.scope: Every body the extension combines with or changes; absent: every body. Allowed without an `operation`, refused with `new`. Since version 11.

import.doc: Geometry read from a file. A STEP file gives a B-rep whose faces are named `import#k:face:<n>` in the file's face order (fragile: imported topology has no history); an STL file gives a mesh, which can only be a reference (display and measure, no B-rep features). Since version 3.

fields.scope: The bodies the operation combines with; absent: every body. Not for `new` or `reference`.

derived.doc: Bodies of a part of another document (or of another version of this one), pinned to a version and carried inside the document. Its bodies are `<id>:from/<source body id>`, and its faces are named `<id>:from/<source face name>`: everything after `:from/` is a name in the source document, never read for this part's feature ids. Since version 6.

fields.bodies: The source part's bodies to derive, by their ids in the source; absent: every body.
fields.scope: The bodies the operation combines with; absent: every body. Not for a `new` feature.

thread.doc: A thread on a cylindrical face: a shaft (external) or a hole (internal), told apart by which side of the face the material is on. It acts on the body that owns the face, like a fillet, so it has no scope. The size is a name of the kernel's thread table; regen refuses one it does not know, so adding sizes never changes the format. Since version 10.

fields.start: A circular edge of the face: the end the thread starts from. Absent: the end nearer the face's first neighbour by name (`cap:end` before `cap:start`: a lone extruded cylinder starts at its top).
fields.length: How far along the face the thread runs from its start; `full`: the whole face.
fields.clearance: Diametral printing clearance, like the fit variables (`#fit_slip`): the thread is this much smaller across (external) or larger (internal) than the basic profile.

scripted.doc: A feature whose geometry a script of the document's library computes (ADR 0010 decision 8). `script` names the script; `params` holds the parameter values by name; `seed` seeds the script's `Math.random` together with the source hash (decision 3), never the feature id, so a remap or a merge never changes geometry; `dependsOn` lists features the script reads by id, as an extension's does. Faces it makes are named `<id>:<operation id>/<name>` (decision 6). Since version 16.
